coverages.description: Live coverage of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest movement — detentions, ultimatums, court cases, INDIA-bloc actions and on-ground developments in Delhi.
coverages.title: CJP Protest 2.0
coverages.current_summary: Dipke was preventively arrested under BNSS Secs 126/170 on Oct 16 ahead of the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at CP Central Park, and on Oct 17 (~4:50 PM IST) the SEM court granted him conditional bail — released on a one-year peace bond plus Rs 50,000 surety. Co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in Tihar (Das in Jail No. 2, Ranka in Jail No. 4 — Indian Express logged them as inmates 3752 and 1784) after their Oct 14 five-day judicial custody; CJP's legal team filed an SEM release application on Oct 17 with a decision expected Oct 18 (single-sourced). The Oct 16 march went ahead as a flash protest near Jantar Mantar with detentions, while Dhruv Rathee's Saturday-noon London rally at Parliament Square on Oct 17 drew polarised supporters and opponents (ANI-confirmed), and Saket Court issued a bailable warrant against Rathee in the 2018 defamation case. Dipke has called a self-pause of CJP street activity till after Diwali (Nov 8).

coverages.description: Live coverage of the Houthi-Saudi escalation — missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and oil sites, airport and airspace closures, Saudi/coalition retaliation, US moves and diplomatic developments.
coverages.title: Houthi-Riyadh Escalation
coverages.current_summary: King Khalid International Airport reopened Oct 17 after its week-long closure, but recovery has stalled — GACA NOTAM A3650/26 (no expiry) still requires prior permission for every flight, and most carriers remain grounded. The coalition announced interceptions Oct 17–19 (drones over Riyadh, missiles at Khamis Mushait); Oct 19 brought the Houthis' deadliest strike since July — three ballistic missiles on the Shabwa training camp killing 73 and injuring 200+. Saudi Arabia lost an AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter in Najran on Oct 18 (technical malfunction, 2 crew killed) while a hostile projectile injured six in Najran homes; Egypt's Sisi sought emergency parliament authorization to defend Saudi Arabia (vote postponed to next Monday); the kingdom postponed next week's 'Davos in the Desert' FII; and Saree claimed six Houthi operations in 48 hours against targets including Riyadh airport, Yanbu, Shaybah and Abha. On Oct 20 the UK announced RAF Typhoon defensive missions over Saudi skies, France sent forces to guard the Yanbu oil terminal and 100+ US advisers fell under a new joint command; inside Yemen, a Houthi strike on a Taiz residential area killed two teenage girls (AP), while the Houthis claimed Saudi airstrikes on fishing boats off Taiz killed eight. Over Oct 20-21 the coalition reported intercepting a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh (destroying its launch platform), five drones and a cruise missile over the Medina region; GCC foreign ministers at the Oct 18 Manama ministerial council condemned the attacks and pushed for a Houthi terrorist designation alongside US-Iran dialogue.

coverages.description: Live coverage of the Russia-Ukraine war focused on the 'Energy Ceasefire' — strikes on energy infrastructure by either side, ceasefire claims and violations, Kremlin/White House/Kyiv statements, EU sanctions and oil-market fallout.
coverages.title: Russia-Ukraine War & Energy Ceasefire
coverages.current_summary: Trump's 'energy ceasefire' is effectively dead: Ukraine resumed refinery strikes Oct 15 — hours after Zelensky told the FT 'the block is out, we're done' — hitting the Rosneft refinery in Ryazan, and on the night of Oct 17–18 launched its largest drone attack of the war on St. Petersburg (~1,000 drones), setting the Petersburg Oil Terminal ablaze. Washington tilted toward Moscow this week: Trump signed an executive order Oct 16 pausing the Graham Act's Russia sanctions (Zelensky called it a 'historic mistake'), and the WSJ reported Putin proposed a Trump–Xi summit on Ukraine — without Kyiv — on the sidelines of the Nov 18–19 APEC summit in Shenzhen (confirmed by the Kremlin Oct 19). On Oct 20, Zelensky met Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, saying US intelligence-sharing 'works now'; Witkoff meets Putin on Wednesday Oct 21. Overnight Oct 19-20, Ukrainian drones struck Transneft's Nikolskoye-1 pumping station in Tambov - a Druzhba-network hub - sparking a fire at a fuel tank (Governor Pervyshov confirmed). On Oct 19 a Russian drone struck a park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv region, killing six including three children, while 22 bipartisan House lawmakers urged Trump (Oct 15 letter) to revoke the Russian diesel import licence.

coverages.description: Live coverage of hurricane and tropical-storm activity impacting North America — NHC advisories, storm formation and intensity changes, watches and warnings, landfalls, casualties, damage and outage numbers, evacuations, closures and recovery.
coverages.location: North America (Atlantic basin, Gulf of Mexico, US Gulf/East coasts, Mexico's Pacific coast)
coverages.title: Hurricane Activity Impacting North America
coverages.current_summary: Tropical Storm Trudy formed off southern Mexico on Oct 13 (40 mph in NHC Advisory 2, ~490 mi SSE of Acapulco) with rapid intensification to a major hurricane forecast by Friday; Hurricane Simon re-strengthened to 110 mph, nearly a major hurricane again, after mainland Mexico watches were lifted (Advisory 26) and Puerto Vallarta airport reopened — NHC's discussion shifted Simon's track to a weekend coast approach with a possible Sunday inland crossing over Sonora; Tropical Storm Trudy (45 mph) had its track nudged east, putting a major-hurricane landfall threat on western Mexico this weekend — while damage tallies keep rising across Guerrero, Colima and Baja California Sur, with Ensenada's death toll from Tropical Cyclone Rachel's remnant flooding reaching 7 on Tuesday Oct 13. The White House approved federal emergency declarations for Florida and Alabama ahead of Isaias's landfall; no active Atlantic cyclones after the Cabo Verde disturbance fizzled. Isaias recovery reached ~95% of impacted-area customers restored as of Tuesday evening (~57,000 still out), Florida rolled out $10M in zero-interest business loans plus farm loans and SNAP aid for the Panhandle, and catastrophe modeler Verisk issued the first industry insured-loss estimate: $1B–$2B for onshore property. DeSantis also raised Florida's storm-related death toll to six; by Wednesday Oct 14 the storm-wide toll reached nine, after the Greenwood County coroner reported 67-year-old Christopher John Miller died Oct 11 when a tree fell on his home in Ninety Six, South Carolina, during Isaias's remnants; by Wednesday morning Oct 14, just over 20,000 customers remained without power — mainly Escambia and Santa Rosa counties — down from 45,000+ Tuesday. Wednesday's NHC updates (Oct 14): Hurricane Simon dipped to 105 mph and drifted southwestward — NHC calls it 'compact' — keeping the weekend coast-approach threat for Sonora; Tropical Storm Trudy strengthened to 50 mph with the track shifted west, and is now expected to reach hurricane strength within 24 hours. Latest NHC advisories (Wed Oct 14, 8-9 AM MST/CST): Hurricane Simon weakened to 90 mph (Category 1), drifting southwestward; Mexico dropped its last coastal watch, leaving no coastal watches or warnings in effect for now, though Baja California Sur watches may be required in the next day or two; Tropical Storm Trudy strengthened to 60 mph and is now expected to become a hurricane tonight and a major hurricane by Friday.

coverages.title: U.S.–Iran Conflict & Strait of Hormuz
coverages.description: Live coverage of the U.S.–Iran confrontation — military posturing, strikes or threats, Strait of Hormuz shipping incidents and closure threats, Iranian statements, US administration moves, oil-market and diplomatic fallout.
coverages.current_summary: Mine warfare in the Strait of Hormuz escalated sharply: the IRGC Navy said two oil tankers (~2M barrels each) were set ablaze by mines on Oct 17 and two more 'non-compliant' tankers on Oct 20, warning oil companies of a 'heavier price'; Kpler counted at least 18 vessel attacks in the fortnight to Oct 20, and Brent touched a five-month high (~$112, settling ~$109) on Oct 20–21. On Oct 19 Iran claimed US forces struck the Konarak naval base wounding two — the first alleged US strike on Iranian soil since Sept 1 — which Washington disputes. Diplomacy crept back on Oct 18: FM Abbas Araqchi said Tehran's offer to reopen the strait within six days remains on the table if Washington lifts the port blockade, ends oil-export sanctions and hostilities; on Oct 21, IMO chief Arsenio Dominguez said mines remain on the approved traffic-separation route and the agency cannot declare it safe. On Oct 20, Iranian armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi warned any renewed attack would draw a 'much stronger and more forceful response', while Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused Iran of 'Nazi U-boat tactics' against commercial shipping and called a deal 'tough'. On Oct 20 Qatar and Pakistan proposed Iran receive the interest earned on ~$6B of frozen funds in Qatari banks in exchange for confidential IAEA inspections; Araghchi said the strait stays closed until Washington accepts Tehran's conditions. On Oct 19 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel, discussing Iran with Netanyahu.

coverages.title: 2026 US Midterm Elections
coverages.description: Polls, early voting, key House/Senate/gubernatorial races, and campaign moves ahead of the Nov 3, 2026 US midterm elections.
coverages.current_summary: Two weeks out, Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 28 House races toward Democrats on Oct 20 — first post-218 projection: Democrats favoured in 223 races, Republicans 200, 12 toss-ups — while the Senate tightens: a CBS News/YouGov poll (Oct 18) has Talarico 51, Paxton 49 in Texas, and Georgia's governor race is effectively tied (AJC/UGA: Jackson 46, Bottoms 45). Trump held his Wichita, KS rally Oct 19 (announcing $8B in one-time farmer payments to offset Iran-war diesel prices) and Greenville, NC Oct 20, part of a cash-pitch closing strategy — $30K government-fraud tips, $5,000 checks if the GOP wins — with Fort Myers, FL (confirmed for Fri Oct 23, plus a second planned Florida rally), Clemson, Iowa, Macon and Lubbock ahead. Early voting is surging: Texas shattered first-day records Oct 19 (Harris County 104,600+ in-person), Georgia passed 1M ballots, Michigan hit 780K; Sanders and O'Rourke kicked off a Texas early-voting tour Oct 19–20 while Talarico held his own events. Georgia GOP governor nominee Rick Jackson will skip Trump's Macon rally on Sat Oct 24, and Barack Obama will headline a 'United for Georgia' rally in Atlanta on Oct 28 for Ossoff and Bottoms.

coverages.description: Live coverage of the French protest movement that began with Paris lycée student blockades in September 2026 and escalated into nationwide cost-of-living demonstrations — marches, clashes, arrests and injuries, union and student actions, government response, and the parliamentary budget fight.
coverages.title: Paris Protests — France Cost-of-Living Unrest
coverages.current_summary: The Oct 17 national day of action (550k–800k nationwide, 110k in Paris) gave way to a post-crisis standoff: Lecornu imposed partial/localized curfews on Oct 19 (Paris protest bans, République 11pm–6am curfew, minors' curfews in several cities) and is meeting union leaders at Matignon on Wednesday Oct 21 (10:30am) and party leaders Thursday Oct 22, while the budget revenue-side vote was postponed to Oct 27. Accountability moves landed Oct 20: Interior Minister Nuñez apologized in the Assembly ('I accept my share of responsibility') as parliament launched an inquiry commission (200 investigators), and the suspected principal arsonist of the Limoges town-hall fire was arrested at dawn by the RAID (SDAT anti-terror co-seized). Ahead of Saturday Oct 24's 'Act II' demos — called by yellow-vest groups (Oct 24 + Oct 31) and backed by five unions striking Nov 5 — Nuñez announced Sentinelle troops, BRI/GIGN/RAID, helicopters and possible bans on non-notified demonstrations. On Oct 20 Toulouse became the first city to impose an all-ages nighttime curfew (hypercentre 11:59 PM-5 AM, Oct 22-25), while Marseille extended its hypercentre/shopping-district curfew (minors 10 PM-5 AM) through Oct 23.
